page: Hetzner Cloud cx33 is a cost-optimized virtual server instance delivering 4 shared AMD EPYC virtual cores operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. Built upon the x86_64 architecture and virtualized via QEMU, the instance is provisioned with 8.0 GB of system memory (approximately 1.95 GB per core) and includes an 80 GB local NVMe SSD. It features 32 KB L1 data cache, 4 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, and SHA-NI for cryptographic efficiency, while AVX-512 and matrix extensions are absent. The instance does not include a dedicated GPU and provisions zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark measurements reflect steady middle-tier compute and memory bandwidth, offset by limitations under heavy parallel compilation. In stress-ng testing, cx33 reaches 2672.38 for single-core and 10641.52 for multi-core performance. PassMark CPU scores evaluate at 8691.84, with encryption operations reaching 4445.72. Memory throughput achieves 470.59 GB/sec for small cached reads, tapering to 67.66 GB/sec for large uncached transfers. Conversely, Geekbench multi-core scores (4356.0) and Clang software compilation (5229.0) land in the lower quartiles, reflecting the impact of shared CPU allocation and modest memory bandwidth. Key-value caching remains responsive, delivering 7.84 million Redis SET operations per second, whereas large-model machine learning inference is restricted by the 8 GB RAM boundary and absence of hardware accelerators.

Operating within a shared-resource model with a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, cx33 prioritizes core density over dedicated throughput. The bundled NVMe SSD provides responsive local storage I/O, though workloads requiring predictable high-sustained compute or large working sets may experience contention due to shared execution. This instance is best suited for budget-sensitive backend services, microservices, staging environments, asynchronous background task workers, and distributed Redis caching nodes.
description: Hetzner Cloud cx33 is a cost-optimized cloud instance configured with 4 shared AMD EPYC virtual cores running at 2.0 GHz, 8 GB of system memory, and 80 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Utilizing x86_64 architecture under the QEMU hypervisor, the server provides hardware encryption support with AES and SHA-NI, alongside AVX vector instructions, while omitting AVX-512. Benchmarks reveal balanced baseline compute, scoring 8691.84 on PassMark CPU and 10641.52 on multi-core stress-ng tests. However, Geekbench multi-core and Clang compilation metrics highlight limitations inherent to shared-core resource contention and memory throughput constraints. In-memory operations achieve steady throughput, demonstrated by 7.84 million Redis SET operations per second, though large-model LLM inference remains constrained. With a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, no integrated GPU, and absent complimentary public IPv4, cx33 delivers economical processing density tailored for development environments, task workers, microservices, and modest web or cache deployments.
